final_message:
The bug was in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`, and it's fixed. The full suite passes, including the new test.

When the gateway declined a charge, `collect` hit an `else: pass` branch and did nothing. It never called `record_failure`, so the subscription never became `past_due` and no retry was scheduled. `record_failure` was only called for a missing or expired card. Now a declined charge calls `record_failure` with the gateway's failure code.

I added your test to `tests/test_lifecycle.py` and wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}`.

steps.command: ls billing tests && wc -l billing/*.py && cat tests/conftest.py && grep -n "past_due\|retry\|def " billing/*.py | head -150
cat billing/dunning.py billing/payments.py; sed -n 85,110p billing/engine.py; grep -n "def transition" -A25 billing/subscriptions.py
grep -rn "record_failure\|recover(" billing; cat billing/gateway.py | sed -n 1,40p; sed -n 36,52p billing/engine.py

python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    else:\n        pass\n","    else:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, result[\"failure_code\"] or \"unknown\")\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_lifecycle.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8
